meta.title: Open CalcSheet Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open CalcSheet Studio: free, open source structural calculations you can read back. Every result shows its formula, numbers and units, and all your sheets become one report. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.

header.label: Structural calculations
header.title: Open CalcSheet Studio
header.tagline: Calculations you can read back, in one report
header.desc: Write your calculation line by line as text, and the app works it out with units and readable formulas. Next to calculation sheets, a project can hold spreadsheets, formula canvases, node graphs, drawings and notebooks. Together they become one report.

alt.hero: A timber joist floor: input screen with drawings and a live unity check next to the worked-out sheet, with the project and the library in the panel
alt.rekenblad: The calculation text next to the worked-out formulas, with every step and its numbers
alt.rapport: The print preview of the report with cover, contents and calculation pages
alt.bladen: A node graph that builds a portal frame, with a 3D preview in the background

notice.text: Try it now: open the app in the browser and choose Module, then Timber joist floor. Change the section or the span and watch the unity check follow.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From calculation line to report
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

calc.title: You can check every step
calc.desc: You write the calculation as text. Every result shows its name, formula, filled-in values and outcome, with units. Change a number and the sheet recalculates while you type.

report.title: One project, one report
report.desc: Cover, table of contents and page numbers run through all sheets, whatever kind they are. With your own logo, colours and font, ready for the project file.

sheets.title: The right sheet for each part
sheets.desc: Text, canvas, spreadsheet, node graph, drawing, notebook, Markdown or PDF, side by side in one project. A drawing or a 3D model can take its sizes from the sheet.

modules.title: Ready-made checks and examples
modules.desc: Modules with an input screen for a timber joist floor, a beam in timber or steel and a two-pile cap, to the Eurocodes with the Dutch national annex. Plus 137 formulas to insert and 15 worked examples.

ifc.title: Your data stays yours
ifc.desc: The project file is IFCX, with every sheet and its text, input and results. You export to IFC4x3, and with the two-pile cap every bar of the cage becomes an IfcReinforcingBar.

units.title: Formulas with units
units.desc: Calculate with mm, kN and N/mm²; the app keeps track of the units.

live.title: Recalculates as you type
live.desc: Change a number and the check follows at once.

lang.title: Conditions, plots and drawings
lang.desc: The calculation language has formulas, conditions, plots and drawings in the sheet.

library.title: 137 formulas
library.desc: Insert a formula with a click, each with a sketch that shows what it is about.

examples.title: 15 worked examples
examples.desc: From the Eurocodes and classical mechanics; corrections reach everyone without a new release.

modules.title: Modules with an input screen
modules.desc: Timber joist floor, beam in timber or steel and two-pile cap. The online module library adds more without a new release.

xlsx.title: Spreadsheet
xlsx.desc: An .xlsx workbook with formulas, cell pointing and fill.

canvas.title: Formula canvas
canvas.desc: Place formulas freely; they calculate top to bottom with the same kernel.

graph.title: Node graph
graph.desc: Nodes for numbers, logic, lists, text and geometry, with a 3D preview. Also reads .dyn graphs.

drawing.title: Drawing
drawing.desc: A4, A3 or A2 with views to scale: grids, levels, walls, steel sections and hollow-core floors.

notebooks.title: Jupyter and Marimo
notebooks.desc: Python notebooks with numpy, scipy, pandas and matplotlib, without installing anything. Tested on the Windows app.

docs.title: Markdown and PDF
docs.desc: Existing text and documents as part of the report.

report.title: One continuous report
report.desc: Cover, contents and page numbers across all sheets, as PDF or through the printer.

style.title: Your own house style
style.desc: The logo, colours and font of your office on the report.

ifc.title: IFCX and IFC4x3
ifc.desc: The project is stored in IFCX; export to IFC4x3 for the BIM model.

import.title: Bring your existing work
import.desc: Opens calculation text (.cpd), workbooks (.xlsx), Markdown and notebooks; DXF becomes a drawing in a sheet.

mcp.title: Works with an AI assistant
mcp.desc: A built-in MCP server and REST API with 43 tools, only on your own computer and behind a token.

notebook.title: Jupyter and Marimo
notebook.desc: Python notebooks as a sheet in your project, with automatic re-running.

graph.title: Node graph

files.a: IFCX projects (.ifccalculation, .ifcx), calculation text (.cpd), workbooks (.xlsx), Markdown, notebooks (.ipynb, .py) and PDF as a sheet. DXF is converted to a drawing in a sheet, and a graph reads .dyn files. IFC4x3 can be exported but not opened.

install.q: Do I have to install anything?
install.a: No, the app also runs in the browser, although file dialogs, saved settings and the Jupyter sheet do not work there. For full use there is a desktop app. It has no built-in updater: install a new version over the old one; your projects stay ordinary files.

cost.a: Nothing. Open CalcSheet Studio is open source under the LGPL-3.0: no licence fees and no account.

format.q: In which file format is my work saved?
format.a: In IFCX, an open format. Every sheet is in it with its text, input and results. You can also export to IFC4x3, .xlsx, Markdown and PDF.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows (x64), macOS (universal, Apple silicon and Intel), Linux (.deb and AppImage) and the browser. Jupyter and Marimo are only tested on Windows, and the report straight to PDF is Windows only; other systems use the print dialog.

practice.a: The modules calculate to EN 1995-1-1, EN 1993-1-1 and EN 1992-1-1 with the Dutch national annex. Every module has a status: the beam and the two-pile cap are "to be checked". The app does not replace the judgment of a structural engineer, so check the results yourself.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: The desktop app has a built-in MCP server and REST API with the same 43 tools: open and save projects, add sheets, set input, calculate, export and print. It only listens on your own computer, behind a token, and you can switch it off or make it read-only.

reliable.a: With every change, 56 check scripts run on Linux and Windows, including 121 results compared against hand calculations. Every result shows its formula and filled-in numbers, so you can follow it yourself.
